units.leftText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the will of God, and Timothy our brother, To the church of God in Corinth, together with all the saints throughout Achaia:
units.rightText: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and Timothy our brother, unto the church of God which is at Corinth, with all the saints that are in the whole of Achaia:

units.leftText: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. The God of All Comfort
units.rightText: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

units.leftText: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassion and the God of all comfort,
units.rightText: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and God of all comfort;

units.leftText: who comforts us in all our troubles, so that we can comfort those in any trouble with the comfort we ourselves have received from God.
units.rightText: who comforteth us in all our affliction, that we may be able to comfort them that are in any affliction, through the comfort wherewith we ourselves are comforted of God.

units.leftText: For just as the sufferings of Christ overflow to us, so also through Christ our comfort overflows.
units.rightText: For as the sufferings of Christ abound unto us, even so our comfort also aboundeth through Christ.

units.leftText: If we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; if we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which accomplishes in you patient endurance of the same sufferings we experience.
units.rightText: But whether we are afflicted, it is for your comfort and salvation; or whether we are comforted, it is for your comfort, which worketh in the patient enduring of the same sufferings which we also suffer:

units.leftText: And our hope for you is sure, because we know that just as you share in our sufferings, so also you will share in our comfort.
units.rightText: and our hope for you is stedfast; knowing that, as ye are partakers of the sufferings, so also are ye of the comfort.

units.leftText: We do not want you to be unaware, brothers, of the hardships we encountered in the province of Asia. We were under a burden far beyond our ability to endure, so that we despaired even of life.
units.rightText: For we would not have you ignorant, brethren, concerning our affliction which befell us in Asia, that we were weighed down exceedingly, beyond our power, insomuch that we despaired even of life:
leftNotes: 1:8 Literally in Asia; Asia was a Roman province in what is now western Turkey.

units.leftText: Indeed, we felt we were under the sentence of death, in order that we would not trust in ourselves, but in God, who raises the dead.
units.rightText: yea, we ourselves have had the sentence of death within ourselves, that we should not trust in ourselves, but in God who raiseth the dead:

units.leftText: He has delivered us from such a deadly peril, and He will deliver us. In Him we have placed our hope that He will yet again deliver us,
units.rightText: who delivered us out of so great a death, and will deliver: on whom we have set our hope that he will also still deliver us;

units.leftText: as you help us by your prayers. Then many will give thanks on our behalf for the favor shown us in answer to their prayers. Paul’s Change of Plans
units.rightText: ye also helping together on our behalf by your supplication; that, for the gift bestowed upon us by means of many, thanks may be given by many persons on our behalf.

units.leftText: For this is our boast: Our conscience testifies that we have conducted ourselves in the world, and especially in relation to you, in the holiness and sincerity that are from God — not in worldly wisdom, but in the grace of God.
units.rightText: For our glorying is this, the testimony of our conscience, that in holiness and sincerity of God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, we behaved ourselves in the world, and more abundantly to you-ward.

units.leftText: For we do not write you anything that is beyond your ability to read and understand. And I hope that you will understand us completely,
units.rightText: For we write no other things unto you, than what ye read or even acknowledge, and I hope ye will acknowledge unto the end:

units.leftText: as you have already understood us in part, that you may boast of us just as we will boast of you in the day of our Lord Jesus.
units.rightText: as also ye did acknowledge us in part, that we are your glorying, even as ye also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.
leftNotes: 1:14 BYZ and TR the Lord Jesus

units.leftText: Confident of this, I planned to visit you first, so that you might receive a double blessing.
units.rightText: And in this confidence I was minded to come first unto you, that ye might have a second benefit;

units.leftText: I wanted to visit you on my way to Macedonia, and to return to you from Macedonia, and then to have you help me on my way to Judea.
units.rightText: and by you to pass into Macedonia, and again from Macedonia to come unto you, and of you to be set forward on my journey unto Judæa.

units.leftText: When I planned this, did I do it carelessly? Or do I make my plans by human standards, so as to say “Yes, yes” and also “No, no”?
units.rightText: When I therefore was thus minded, did I show fickleness? or the things that I purpose, do I purpose according to the flesh, that with me there should be the yea yea and the nay nay?

units.leftText: But as surely as God is faithful, our message to you is not “Yes” and “No.”
units.rightText: But as God is faithful, our word toward you is not yea and nay.

units.leftText: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not “Yes” and “No,” but in Him it has always been “Yes.”
units.rightText: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was preached among you by us, even by me and Silvanus and Timothy, was not yea and nay, but in him is yea.

units.leftText: For all the promises of God are “Yes” in Christ. And so through Him, our “Amen” is spoken to the glory of God.
units.rightText: For how many soever be the promises of God, in him is the yea: wherefore also through him is the Amen, unto the glory of God through us.

units.leftText: Now it is God who establishes both us and you in Christ. He anointed us,
units.rightText: Now he that establisheth us with you in Christ, and anointed us, is God;

units.leftText: placed His seal on us, and put His Spirit in our hearts as a pledge of what is to come.
units.rightText: who also sealed us, and gave us the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.

units.leftText: I call God as my witness that it was in order to spare you that I did not return to Corinth.
units.rightText: But I call God for a witness upon my soul, that to spare you I forbare to come unto Corinth.

units.leftText: Not that we lord it over your faith, but we are fellow workers with you for your joy, because it is by faith that you stand firm.
units.rightText: Not that we have lordship over your faith, but are helpers of your joy: for in faith ye stand fast.

units.leftText: So I made up my mind not to make another painful visit to you.
units.rightText: But I determined this for myself, that I would not come again to you with sorrow.

units.leftText: For if I grieve you, who is left to cheer me but those whom I have grieved?
units.rightText: For if I make you sorry, who then is he that maketh me glad but he that is made sorry by me?

units.leftText: I wrote as I did so that on my arrival I would not be grieved by those who ought to make me rejoice. I had confidence in all of you, that you would share my joy.
units.rightText: And I wrote this very thing, lest, when I came, I should have sorrow from them of whom I ought to rejoice; having confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.

units.leftText: For through many tears I wrote you out of great distress and anguish of heart, not to grieve you but to let you know how much I love you.
units.rightText: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote unto you with many tears; not that ye should be made sorry, but that ye might know the love which I have more abundantly unto you.

units.leftText: Now if anyone has caused grief, he has not grieved me but all of you — to some degree, not to overstate it.
units.rightText: But if any hath caused sorrow, he hath caused sorrow, not to me, but in part (that I press not too heavily) to you all.

units.leftText: The punishment imposed on him by the majority is sufficient for him.
units.rightText: Sufficient to such a one is this punishment which was inflicted by the many;

units.leftText: So instead, you ought to forgive and comfort him, so that he will not be overwhelmed by excessive sorrow.
units.rightText: so that contrariwise ye should rather forgive him and comfort him, lest by any means such a one should be swallowed up with his overmuch sorrow.

units.leftText: Therefore I urge you to reaffirm your love for him.
units.rightText: Wherefore I beseech you to confirm your love toward him.

units.leftText: My purpose in writing you was to see if you would stand the test and be obedient in everything.
units.rightText: For to this end also did I write, that I might know the proof of you, whether ye are obedient in all things.

units.leftText: If you forgive anyone, I also forgive him. And if I have forgiven anything, I have forgiven it in the presence of Christ for your sake,
units.rightText: But to whom ye forgive anything, I forgive also: for what I also have forgiven, if I have forgiven anything, for your sakes have I forgiven it in the presence of Christ;

units.leftText: in order that Satan should not outwit us. For we are not unaware of his schemes. Triumph in Christ
units.rightText: that no advantage may be gained over us by Satan: for we are not ignorant of his devices.

units.leftText: Now when I went to Troas to preach the gospel of Christ and a door stood open for me in the Lord,
units.rightText: Now when I came to Troas for the gospel of Christ, and when a door was opened unto me in the Lord,

units.leftText: I had no peace in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus there. So I said goodbye to them and went on to Macedonia.
units.rightText: I had no relief for my spirit, because I found not Titus my brother: but taking my leave of them, I went forth into Macedonia.

units.leftText: But thanks be to God, who always leads us triumphantly as captives in Christ and through us spreads everywhere the fragrance of the knowledge of Him.
units.rightText: But thanks be unto God, who always leadeth us in triumph in Christ, and maketh manifest through us the savor of his knowledge in every place.

units.leftText: For we are to God the sweet aroma of Christ among those who are being saved and those who are perishing.
units.rightText: For we are a sweet savor of Christ unto God, in them that are saved, and in them that perish;

units.leftText: To the one we are an odor that brings death, to the other a fragrance that brings life. And who is qualified for such a task?
units.rightText: to the one a savor from death unto death; to the other a savor from life unto life. And who is sufficient for these things?
leftNotes: 2:16 Literally To the one, indeed, an aroma from death to death; but to the other, an aroma from life to life.

units.leftText: For we are not like so many others, who peddle the word of God for profit. On the contrary, in Christ we speak before God with sincerity, as men sent from God.
units.rightText: For we are not as the many, corrupting the word of God: but as of sincerity, but as of God, in the sight of God, speak we in Christ.

units.leftText: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?
units.rightText: Are we beginning again to commend ourselves? or need we, as do some, epistles of commendation to you or from you?

units.leftText: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.
units.rightText: Ye are our epistle, written in our hearts, known and read of all men;

units.leftText: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.
units.rightText: being made manifest that ye are an epistle of Christ, ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in tables that are hearts of flesh.

units.leftText: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.
units.rightText: And such confidence have we through Christ to God-ward:

units.leftText: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.
units.rightText: not that we are sufficient of ourselves, to account anything as from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God;

units.leftText: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life. The Glory of the New Covenant (Exodus 34:10–35|EXO 34:10-35*)
units.rightText: who also made us sufficient as ministers of a new covenant; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.

units.leftText: Now if the ministry of death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory,
units.rightText: But if the ministration of death, written, and engraven on stones, came with glory, so that the children of Israel could not look stedfastly upon the face of Moses for the glory of his face; which glory was passing away:

units.leftText: will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?
units.rightText: how shall not rather the ministration of the spirit be with glory?

units.leftText: For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!
units.rightText: For if the ministration of condemnation hath glory, much rather doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

units.leftText: Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.
units.rightText: For verily that which hath been made glorious hath not been made glorious in this respect, by reason of the glory that surpasseth.

units.leftText: For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!
units.rightText: For if that which passeth away was with glory, much more that which remaineth is in glory.

units.leftText: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.
units.rightText: Having therefore such a hope, we use great boldness of speech,

units.leftText: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.
units.rightText: and are not as Moses, who put a veil upon his face, that the children of Israel should not look stedfastly on the end of that which was passing away:

units.leftText: But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.
units.rightText: but their minds were hardened: for until this very day at the reading of the old covenant the same veil remaineth, it not being revealed to them that it is done away in Christ.

units.leftText: And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.
units.rightText: But unto this day, whensoever Moses is read, a veil lieth upon their heart.

units.leftText: But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
units.rightText: But whensoever it shall turn to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

units.leftText: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.
units.rightText: Now the Lord is the Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

units.leftText: And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
units.rightText: But we all, with unveiled face beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord the Spirit.

units.leftText: Therefore, since God in His mercy has given us this ministry, we do not lose heart.
units.rightText: Therefore seeing we have this ministry, even as we obtained mercy, we faint not:
leftNotes: 4:1 Literally Therefore, having this ministry, as we have received mercy,

units.leftText: Instead, we have renounced secret and shameful ways. We do not practice deceit, nor do we distort the word of God. On the contrary, by open proclamation of the truth, we commend ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.
units.rightText: but we have renounced the hidden things of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor handling the word of God deceitfully; but by the manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every man’s conscience in the sight of God.

units.leftText: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who are perishing.
units.rightText: And even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled in them that perish:

units.leftText: The god of this age has blinded the minds of unbelievers, so they cannot see the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God.
units.rightText: in whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of the unbelieving, that the light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should not dawn upon them.

units.leftText: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Jesus Christ as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.
units.rightText: For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for Jesus’ sake.

units.leftText: For God, who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” made His light shine in our hearts to give us the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. Treasure in Jars of Clay (Romans 6:1–14|ROM 6:1-14*)
units.rightText: Seeing it is God, that said, Light shall shine out of darkness, who shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
leftNotes: 4:6 SBL, NE, and WH in the face of Christ

units.leftText: Now we have this treasure in jars of clay to show that this surpassingly great power is from God and not from us.
units.rightText: But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the exceeding greatness of the power may be of God, and not from ourselves;

units.leftText: We are hard pressed on all sides, but not crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;
units.rightText: we are pressed on every side, yet not straitened; perplexed, yet not unto despair;

units.leftText: persecuted, but not forsaken; struck down, but not destroyed.
units.rightText: pursued, yet not forsaken; smitten down, yet not destroyed;

units.leftText: We always carry around in our body the death of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our body.
units.rightText: always bearing about in the body the dying of Jesus, that the life also of Jesus may be manifested in our body.

units.leftText: For we who are alive are always consigned to death for Jesus’ sake, so that the life of Jesus may also be revealed in our mortal body.
units.rightText: For we who live are always delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus may be manifested in our mortal flesh.

units.leftText: So then, death is at work in us, but life is at work in you.
units.rightText: So then death worketh in us, but life in you.

units.leftText: And in keeping with what is written, “I believed, therefore I have spoken,” we who have the same spirit of faith also believe and therefore speak,
units.rightText: But having the same spirit of faith, according to that which is written, I believed, and therefore did I speak; we also believe, and therefore also we speak;

units.leftText: knowing that the One who raised the Lord Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us with you in His presence.
units.rightText: knowing that he that raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also with Jesus, and shall present us with you.

units.leftText: All this is for your benefit, so that the grace that is extending to more and more people may cause thanksgiving to overflow, to the glory of God.
units.rightText: For all things are for your sakes, that the grace, being multiplied through the many, may cause the thanksgiving to abound unto the glory of God.

units.leftText: Therefore we do not lose heart. Though our outer self is wasting away, yet our inner self is being renewed day by day.
units.rightText: Wherefore we faint not; but though our outward man is decaying, yet our inward man is renewed day by day.

units.leftText: For our light and momentary affliction is producing for us an eternal weight of glory that is far beyond comparison.
units.rightText: For our light affliction, which is for the moment, worketh for us more and more exceedingly an eternal weight of glory;

units.leftText: So we fix our eyes not on what is seen, but on what is unseen. For what is seen is temporary, but what is unseen is eternal.
units.rightText: while we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

units.leftText: For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is dismantled, we have a building from God, an eternal house in heaven, not built by human hands.
units.rightText: For we know that if the earthly house of our tabernacle be dissolved, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal, in the heavens.

units.leftText: For in this tent we groan, longing to be clothed with our heavenly dwelling,
units.rightText: For verily in this we groan, longing to be clothed upon with our habitation which is from heaven:

units.leftText: because when we are clothed, we will not be found naked.
units.rightText: if so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.

units.leftText: For while we are in this tent, we groan under our burdens, because we do not wish to be unclothed but clothed, so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life.
units.rightText: For indeed we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened; not for that we would be unclothed, but that we would be clothed upon, that what is mortal may be swallowed up of life.

units.leftText: And it is God who has prepared us for this very purpose and has given us the Spirit as a pledge of what is to come.
units.rightText: Now he that wrought us for this very thing is God, who gave unto us the earnest of the Spirit.

units.leftText: Therefore we are always confident, although we know that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord.
units.rightText: Being therefore always of good courage, and knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord

units.leftText: For we walk by faith, not by sight.
units.rightText: (for we walk by faith, not by sight);

units.leftText: We are confident, then, and would prefer to be away from the body and at home with the Lord.
units.rightText: we are of good courage, I say, and are willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be at home with the Lord.

units.leftText: So we aspire to please Him, whether we are at home in this body or away from it.
units.rightText: Wherefore also we make it our aim, whether at home or absent, to be well-pleasing unto him.

units.leftText: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive his due for the things done in the body, whether good or bad. Ambassadors for Christ
units.rightText: For we must all be made manifest before the judgment-seat of Christ; that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he hath done, whether it be good or bad.

units.leftText: Therefore, since we know what it means to fear the Lord, we try to persuade men. What we are is clear to God, and I hope it is clear to your conscience as well.
units.rightText: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men, but we are made manifest unto God; and I hope that we are made manifest also in your consciences.

units.leftText: We are not commending ourselves to you again. Instead, we are giving you an occasion to be proud of us, so that you can answer those who take pride in appearances rather than in the heart.
units.rightText: We are not again commending ourselves unto you, but speak as giving you occasion of glorying on our behalf, that ye may have wherewith to answer them that glory in appearance, and not in heart.

units.leftText: If we are out of our mind, it is for God; if we are of sound mind, it is for you.
units.rightText: For whether we are beside ourselves, it is unto God; or whether we are of sober mind, it is unto you.

units.leftText: For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that One died for all, therefore all died.
units.rightText: For the love of Christ constraineth us; because we thus judge, that one died for all, therefore all died;

units.leftText: And He died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for them and was raised again.
units.rightText: and he died for all, that they that live should no longer live unto themselves, but unto him who for their sakes died and rose again.

units.leftText: So from now on we regard no one according to the flesh. Although we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer.
units.rightText: Wherefore we henceforth know no man after the flesh: even though we have known Christ after the flesh, yet now we know him so no more.

units.leftText: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!
units.rightText: Wherefore if any man is in Christ, he is a new creature: the old things are passed away; behold, they are become new.

units.leftText: All this is from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation:
units.rightText: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ, and gave unto us the ministry of reconciliation;

units.leftText: that God was reconciling the world to Himself in Christ, not counting men’s trespasses against them. And He has committed to us the message of reconciliation.
units.rightText: to wit, that God was in Christ reconciling the world unto himself, not reckoning unto them their trespasses, and having committed unto us the word of reconciliation.

units.leftText: Therefore we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us. We implore you on behalf of Christ: Be reconciled to God.
units.rightText: We are ambassadors therefore on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beseech you on behalf of Christ, be ye reconciled to God.

units.leftText: God made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
units.rightText: Him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf; that we might become the righteousness of God in him.

units.leftText: As God’s fellow workers, then, we urge you not to receive God’s grace in vain.
units.rightText: And working together with him we entreat also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain

units.leftText: For He says: “In the time of favor I heard you, and in the day of salvation I helped you.” Behold, now is the time of favor; now is the day of salvation!
units.rightText: (for he saith, At an acceptable time I hearkened unto thee, And in a day of salvation did I succor thee: behold, now is the acceptable time; behold, now is the day of salvation):

units.leftText: We put no obstacle in anyone’s way, so that no one can discredit our ministry.
units.rightText: giving no occasion of stumbling in anything, that our ministration be not blamed;

units.leftText: Rather, as servants of God we commend ourselves in every way: in great endurance; in troubles, hardships, and calamities;
units.rightText: but in everything commending ourselves, as ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses,

units.leftText: in beatings, imprisonments, and riots; in labor, sleepless nights, and hunger;
units.rightText: in stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labors, in watchings, in fastings;

units.leftText: in purity, knowledge, patience, and kindness; in the Holy Spirit and in sincere love;
units.rightText: in pureness, in knowledge, in longsuffering, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in love unfeigned,

units.leftText: in truthful speech and in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness in the right hand and in the left;
units.rightText: in the word of truth, in the power of God; by the armor of righteousness on the right hand and on the left,

units.leftText: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;
units.rightText: by glory and dishonor, by evil report and good report; as deceivers, and yet true;

units.leftText: unknown, yet well-known; dying, and yet we live on; punished, yet not killed;
units.rightText: as unknown, and yet well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as chastened, and not killed;

units.leftText: sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; poor, yet making many rich; having nothing, and yet possessing everything.
units.rightText: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing all things.

units.leftText: We have spoken freely to you, Corinthians. Our hearts are open wide.
units.rightText: Our mouth is open unto you, O Corinthians, our heart is enlarged.

units.leftText: It is not our affection, but yours, that is restrained.
units.rightText: Ye are not straitened in us, but ye are straitened in your own affections.

units.leftText: As a fair exchange— I speak as to my children— open wide your hearts also. Do Not Be Unequally Yoked
units.rightText: Now for a recompense in like kind (I speak as unto my children), be ye also enlarged.

units.leftText: Do not be unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership can righteousness have with wickedness? Or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
units.rightText: Be not unequally yoked with unbelievers: for what fellowship have righteousness and iniquity? or what communion hath light with darkness?

units.leftText: What harmony is there between Christ and Belial? Or what does a believer have in common with an unbeliever?
units.rightText: And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what portion hath a believer with an unbeliever?
leftNotes: 6:15 Scrivener’s TR and PT; many Greek sources Beliar

units.leftText: What agreement can exist between the temple of God and idols? For we are the temple of the living God. As God has said: “I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people.”
units.rightText: And what agreement hath a temple of God with idols? for we are a temple of the living God; even as God said, I will dwell in them, and walk in them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

units.leftText: “Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord. Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you.”
units.rightText: Wherefore Come ye out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, And touch no unclean thing; And I will receive you,
leftNotes: 6:17 Isaiah 52:11|ISA 52:11*; see also Ezekiel 20:34, including LXX.

units.leftText: And: “I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty.”
units.rightText: And will be to you a Father, And ye shall be to me sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.

units.leftText: Therefore, beloved, since we have these promises, let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
units.rightText: Having therefore these promises, beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.

units.leftText: Make room for us in your hearts. We have wronged no one, we have corrupted no one, we have exploited no one.
units.rightText: Open your hearts to us: we wronged no man, we corrupted no man, we took advantage of no man.

units.leftText: I do not say this to condemn you. I have said before that you so occupy our hearts that we live and die together with you.
units.rightText: I say it not to condemn you: for I have said before, that ye are in our hearts to die together and live together.

units.leftText: Great is my confidence in you; great is my pride in you; I am filled with encouragement; in all our troubles my joy overflows.
units.rightText: Great is my boldness of speech toward you, great is my glorying on your behalf: I am filled with comfort, I overflow with joy in all our affliction.

units.leftText: For when we arrived in Macedonia, our bodies had no rest, but we were pressed from every direction — conflicts on the outside, fears within.
units.rightText: For even when we were come into Macedonia our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.

units.leftText: But God, who comforts the downcast, comforted us by the arrival of Titus,
units.rightText: Nevertheless he that comforteth the lowly, even God, comforted us by the coming of Titus;

units.leftText: and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort he had received from you. He told us about your longing, your mourning, and your zeal for me, so that I rejoiced all the more.
units.rightText: and not by his coming only, but also by the comfort wherewith he was comforted in you, while he told us your longing, your mourning, your zeal for me; so that I rejoiced yet more.

units.leftText: Even if I caused you sorrow by my letter, I do not regret it. Although I did regret it— for I see that my letter caused you sorrow, but only for a short time—
units.rightText: For though I made you sorry with my epistle, I do not regret it: though I did regret it (for I see that that epistle made you sorry, though but for a season),

units.leftText: yet now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because your sorrow led you to repentance. For you felt the sorrow that God had intended, and so were not harmed in any way by us.
units.rightText: I now rejoice, not that ye were made sorry, but that ye were made sorry unto repentance; for ye were made sorry after a godly sort, that ye might suffer loss by us in nothing.

units.leftText: Godly sorrow brings repentance that leads to salvation without regret, but worldly sorrow brings death.
units.rightText: For godly sorrow worketh repentance unto salvation, a repentance which bringeth no regret: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.

units.leftText: Consider what this godly sorrow has produced in you: what earnestness, what eagerness to clear yourselves, what indignation, what alarm, what longing, what zeal, what vindication! In every way you have proved yourselves to be innocent in this matter.
units.rightText: For behold, this selfsame thing, that ye were made sorry after a godly sort, what earnest care it wrought in you, yea what clearing of yourselves, yea what indignation, yea what fear, yea what longing, yea what zeal, yea what avenging! In everything ye approved yourselves to be pure in the matter.

units.leftText: So even though I wrote to you, it was not on account of the one who did wrong or the one who was harmed, but rather that your earnestness on our behalf would be made clear to you in the sight of God.
units.rightText: So although I wrote unto you, I wrote not for his cause that did the wrong, nor for his cause that suffered the wrong, but that your earnest care for us might be made manifest unto you in the sight of God.

units.leftText: On account of this, we are encouraged.
units.rightText: Therefore we have been comforted: and in our comfort we joyed the more exceedingly for the joy of Titus, because his spirit hath been refreshed by you all.

units.leftText: Indeed, I was not embarrassed by anything I had boasted to him about you. But just as everything we said to you was true, so our boasting to Titus has proved to be true as well.
units.rightText: For if in anything I have gloried to him on your behalf, I was not put to shame; but as we spake all things to you in truth, so our glorying also which I made before Titus was found to be truth.

units.leftText: And his affection for you is even greater when he remembers that you were all obedient as you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
units.rightText: And his affection is more abundantly toward you, while he remembereth the obedience of you all, how with fear and trembling ye received him.

units.leftText: I rejoice that I can have complete confidence in you.
units.rightText: I rejoice that in everything I am of good courage concerning you.

units.leftText: Now, brothers, we want you to know about the grace that God has given the churches of Macedonia.
units.rightText: Moreover, brethren, we make known to you the grace of God which hath been given in the churches of Macedonia;

units.leftText: In the terrible ordeal they suffered, their abundant joy and deep poverty overflowed into rich generosity.
units.rightText: how that in much proof of affliction the abundance of their joy and their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality.

units.leftText: For I testify that they gave according to their ability and even beyond it. Of their own accord,
units.rightText: For according to their power, I bear witness, yea and beyond their power, they gave of their own accord,

units.leftText: they earnestly pleaded with us for the privilege of sharing in this service to the saints.
units.rightText: beseeching us with much entreaty in regard of this grace and the fellowship in the ministering to the saints:

units.leftText: And not only did they do as we expected, but they gave themselves first to the Lord and then to us, through the will of God.
units.rightText: and this, not as we had hoped, but first they gave their own selves to the Lord, and to us through the will of God.

units.leftText: So we urged Titus to help complete your act of grace, just as he had started it.
units.rightText: Insomuch that we exhorted Titus, that as he had made a beginning before, so he would also complete in you this grace also.

units.leftText: But just as you excel in everything — in faith, in speech, in knowledge, in complete earnestness, and in the love we inspired in you — see that you also excel in this grace of giving.
units.rightText: But as ye abound in everything, in faith, and utterance, and knowledge, and in all earnestness, and in your love to us, see that ye abound in this grace also.
leftNotes: 8:7 Or in your love for us

units.leftText: I am not giving a command, but I am testing the sincerity of your love through the earnestness of others.
units.rightText: I speak not by way of commandment, but as proving through the earnestness of others the sincerity also of your love.

units.leftText: For you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though He was rich, yet for your sake He became poor, so that you through His poverty might become rich.
units.rightText: For ye know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that, though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, that ye through his poverty might become rich.

units.leftText: And this is my opinion about what is helpful for you in this matter: Last year you were the first not only to give, but even to have such a desire.
units.rightText: And herein I give my judgment: for this is expedient for you, who were the first to make a beginning a year ago, not only to do, but also to will.

units.leftText: Now finish the work, so that you may complete it with the same eager desire, according to your means.
units.rightText: But now complete the doing also; that as there was the readiness to will, so there may be the completion also out of your ability.

units.leftText: For if the eagerness is there, the gift is acceptable according to what one has, not according to what he does not have.
units.rightText: For if the readiness is there, it is acceptable according as a man hath, not according as he hath not.

units.leftText: It is not our intention that others may be relieved while you are burdened, but that there may be equality.
units.rightText: For I say not this that others may be eased and ye distressed;

units.leftText: At the present time, your surplus will meet their need, so that in turn their surplus will meet your need. This way there will be equality.
units.rightText: but by equality: your abundance being a supply at this present time for their want, that their abundance also may become a supply for your want; that there may be equality:

units.leftText: As it is written: “He who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall.” Titus Commended (Titus 1:1–4|TIT 1:1-4*)
units.rightText: as it is written, He that gathered much had nothing over; and he that gathered little had no lack.

units.leftText: But thanks be to God, who put into the heart of Titus the same devotion I have for you.
units.rightText: But thanks be to God, who putteth the same earnest care for you into the heart of Titus.

units.leftText: For not only did he welcome our appeal, but he is eagerly coming to you of his own volition.
units.rightText: For he accepted indeed our exhortation; but being himself very earnest, he went forth unto you of his own accord.

units.leftText: Along with Titus we are sending the brother who is praised by all the churches for his work in the gospel.
units.rightText: And we have sent together with him the brother whose praise in the gospel is spread through all the churches;

units.leftText: More than that, this brother was chosen by the churches to accompany us with the gracious offering we administer to honor the Lord Himself and to show our eagerness to help.
units.rightText: and not only so, but who was also appointed by the churches to travel with us in the matter of this grace, which is ministered by us to the glory of the Lord, and to show our readiness:

units.leftText: We want to avoid any criticism of the way we administer this generous gift.
units.rightText: avoiding this, that any man should blame us in the matter of this bounty which is ministered by us:

units.leftText: For we are taking great care to do what is right, not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men.
units.rightText: for we take thought for things honorable, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.

units.leftText: And we are sending along with them our brother who has proven his earnestness to us many times and in many ways, and now even more so by his great confidence in you.
units.rightText: And we have sent with them our brother, whom we have many times proved earnest in many things, but now much more earnest, by reason of the great confidence which he hath in you.

units.leftText: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow worker among you. As for our brothers, they are messengers of the churches, the glory of Christ.
units.rightText: Whether any inquire about Titus, he is my partner and my fellow-worker to you-ward; or our brethren, they are the messengers of the churches, they are the glory of Christ.

units.leftText: In full view of the churches, then, show these men the proof of your love and the reason for our boasting about you.
units.rightText: Show ye therefore unto them in the face of the churches the proof of your love, and of our glorying on your behalf.

units.leftText: Now about the service to the saints, there is no need for me to write to you.
units.rightText: For as touching the ministering to the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you:

units.leftText: For I know your eagerness to help, and I have been boasting to the Macedonians that since last year you in Achaia were prepared to give. And your zeal has stirred most of them to do likewise.
units.rightText: for I know your readiness, of which I glory on your behalf to them of Macedonia, that Achaia hath been prepared for a year past; and your zeal hath stirred up very many of them.

units.leftText: But I am sending the brothers in order that our boasting about you in this matter should not prove empty, but that you will be prepared, just as I said.
units.rightText: But I have sent the brethren, that our glorying on your behalf may not be made void in this respect; that, even as I said, ye may be prepared:

units.leftText: Otherwise, if any Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we — to say nothing of you — would be ashamed of having been so confident.
units.rightText: lest by any means, if there come with me any of Macedonia and find you unprepared, we (that we say not, ye) should be put to shame in this confidence.

units.leftText: So I thought it necessary to urge the brothers to visit you beforehand and make arrangements for the generous gift you had promised. This way, your gift will be prepared generously and not begrudgingly.
units.rightText: I thought it necessary therefore to entreat the brethren, that they would go before unto you, and make up beforehand your aforepromised bounty, that the same might be ready as a matter of bounty, and not of extortion.

units.leftText: Remember this: Whoever sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and whoever sows generously will also reap generously.
units.rightText: But this I say, He that soweth sparingly shall reap also sparingly; and he that soweth bountifully shall reap also bountifully.

units.leftText: Each one should give what he has decided in his heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
units.rightText: Let each man do according as he hath purposed in his heart: not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver.

units.leftText: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that in all things, at all times, having all that you need, you will abound in every good work.
units.rightText: And God is able to make all grace abound unto you; that ye, having always all sufficiency in everything, may abound unto every good work:

units.leftText: As it is written: “He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.”
units.rightText: as it is written, He hath scattered abroad, he hath given to the poor; His righteousness abideth for ever.

units.leftText: Now He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your store of seed and will increase the harvest of your righteousness.
units.rightText: And he that supplieth seed to the sower and bread for food, shall supply and multiply your seed for sowing, and increase the fruits of your righteousness:

units.leftText: You will be enriched in every way to be generous on every occasion, and through us your generosity will produce thanksgiving to God.
units.rightText: ye being enriched in everything unto all liberality, which worketh through us thanksgiving to God.

units.leftText: For this ministry of service is not only supplying the needs of the saints but is also overflowing in many expressions of thanksgiving to God.
units.rightText: For the ministration of this service not only filleth up the measure of the wants of the saints, but aboundeth also through many thanksgivings unto God;

units.leftText: Because of the proof this ministry provides, the saints will glorify God for your obedient confession of the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your contribution to them and to all the others.
units.rightText: seeing that through the proving of you by this ministration they glorify God for the obedience of your confession unto the gospel of Christ, and for the liberality of your contribution unto them and unto all;

units.leftText: And their prayers for you will express their affection for you, because of the surpassing grace God has given you.
units.rightText: while they themselves also, with supplication on your behalf, long after you by reason of the exceeding grace of God in you.

units.leftText: Thanks be to God for His indescribable gift!
units.rightText: Thanks be to God for his unspeakable gift.

units.leftText: Now by the mildness and gentleness of Christ, I appeal to you — I, Paul, who am humble when face to face with you, but bold when away.
units.rightText: Now I Paul myself entreat you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ, I who in your presence am lowly among you, but being absent am of good courage toward you:

units.leftText: I beg you that when I come I may not need to be as bold as I expect toward those who presume that we live according to the flesh.
units.rightText: yea, I beseech you, that I may not when present show courage with the confidence wherewith I count to be bold against some, who count of us as if we walked according to the flesh.

units.leftText: For though we live in the flesh, we do not wage war according to the flesh.
units.rightText: For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war according to the flesh

units.leftText: The weapons of our warfare are not the weapons of the flesh. Instead, they have divine power to demolish strongholds.
units.rightText: (for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God to the casting down of strongholds);

units.leftText: We demolish arguments and every presumption set up against the knowledge of God; and we take captive every thought to make it obedient to Christ.
units.rightText: casting down imaginations, and every high thing that is exalted against the knowledge of God, and bringing every thought into captivity to the obedience of Christ;

units.leftText: And we will be ready to punish every act of disobedience, as soon as your obedience is complete.
units.rightText: and being in readiness to avenge all disobedience, when your obedience shall be made full.

units.leftText: You are looking at outward appearances. If anyone is confident that he belongs to Christ, he should remind himself that we belong to Christ just as much as he does.
units.rightText: Ye look at the things that are before your face. If any man trusteth in himself that he is Christ’s, let him consider this again with himself, that, even as he is Christ’s, so also are we.

units.leftText: For even if I boast somewhat excessively about the authority the Lord gave us for building you up rather than tearing you down, I will not be ashamed.
units.rightText: For though I should glory somewhat abundantly concerning our authority (which the Lord gave for building you up, and not for casting you down), I shall not be put to shame:

units.leftText: I do not want to seem to be trying to frighten you by my letters.
units.rightText: that I may not seem as if I would terrify you by my letters.

units.leftText: For some say, “His letters are weighty and forceful, but his physical presence is unimpressive, and his speaking is of no account.”
units.rightText: For, His letters, they say, are weighty and strong; but his bodily presence is weak, and his speech of no account.

units.leftText: Such people should consider that what we are in our letters when absent, we will be in our actions when present.
units.rightText: Let such a one reckon this, that, what we are in word by letters when we are absent, such are we also in deed when we are present.

units.leftText: We do not dare to classify or compare ourselves with some who commend themselves. When they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they show their ignorance.
units.rightText: For we are not bold to number or compare ourselves with certain of them that commend themselves: but they themselves, measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves, are without understanding.

units.leftText: We, however, will not boast beyond our limits, but only within the field of influence that God has assigned to us — a field that reaches even to you.
units.rightText: But we will not glory beyond our measure, but according to the measure of the province which God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even unto you.

units.leftText: We are not overstepping our bounds, as if we had not come to you. Indeed, we were the first to reach you with the gospel of Christ.
units.rightText: For we stretch not ourselves overmuch, as though we reached not unto you: for we came even as far as unto you in the gospel of Christ:

units.leftText: Neither do we boast beyond our limits in the labors of others. But we hope that as your faith increases, our area of influence among you will greatly increase as well,
units.rightText: not glorying beyond our measure, that is, in other men’s labors; but having hope that, as your faith groweth, we shall be magnified in you according to our province unto further abundance,

units.leftText: so that we can preach the gospel in the regions beyond you. Then we will not be boasting in the work already done in another man’s territory.
units.rightText: so as to preach the gospel even unto the parts beyond you, and not to glory in another’s province in regard of things ready to our hand.

units.leftText: Rather, “Let him who boasts boast in the Lord.”
units.rightText: But he that glorieth, let him glory in the Lord.

units.leftText: For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
units.rightText: For not he that commendeth himself is approved, but whom the Lord commendeth.

units.leftText: I hope you will put up with a little of my foolishness, but you are already doing that.
units.rightText: Would that ye could bear with me in a little foolishness: but indeed ye do bear with me.

units.leftText: I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy. For I promised you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ.
units.rightText: For I am jealous over you with a godly jealousy: for I espoused you to one husband, that I might present you as a pure virgin to Christ.

units.leftText: I am afraid, however, that just as Eve was deceived by the serpent’s cunning, your minds may be led astray from your simple and pure devotion to Christ.
units.rightText: But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve in his craftiness, your minds should be corrupted from the simplicity and the purity that is toward Christ.

units.leftText: For if someone comes and proclaims a Jesus other than the One we proclaimed, or if you receive a different spirit than the One you received, or a different gospel than the one you accepted, you put up with it very easily.
units.rightText: For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus, whom we did not preach, or if ye receive a different spirit, which ye did not receive, or a different gospel, which ye did not accept, ye do well to bear with him.

units.leftText: I consider myself in no way inferior to those “super-apostles.”
units.rightText: For I reckon that I am not a whit behind the very chiefest apostles.

units.leftText: Although I am not a polished speaker, I am certainly not lacking in knowledge. We have made this clear to you in every way possible.
units.rightText: But though I be rude in speech, yet am I not in knowledge; nay, in every way have we made this manifest unto you in all things.

units.leftText: Was it a sin for me to humble myself in order to exalt you, because I preached the gospel of God to you free of charge?
units.rightText: Or did I commit a sin in abasing myself that ye might be exalted, because I preached to you the gospel of God for nought?

units.leftText: I robbed other churches by accepting their support in order to serve you.
units.rightText: I robbed other churches, taking wages of them that I might minister unto you;

units.leftText: And when I was with you and in need, I was not a burden to anyone; for the brothers who came from Macedonia supplied my needs. I have refrained from being a burden to you in any way, and I will continue to do so.
units.rightText: and when I was present with you and was in want, I was not a burden on any man; for the brethren, when they came from Macedonia, supplied the measure of my want; and in everything I kept myself from being burdensome unto you, and so will I keep myself.

units.leftText: As surely as the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine will not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
units.rightText: As the truth of Christ is in me, no man shall stop me of this glorying in the regions of Achaia.

units.leftText: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows I do!
units.rightText: Wherefore? because I love you not? God knoweth.

units.leftText: But I will keep on doing what I am doing, in order to undercut those who want an opportunity to be regarded as our equals in the things of which they boast.
units.rightText: But what I do, that I will do, that I may cut off occasion from them that desire an occasion; that wherein they glory, they may be found even as we.

units.leftText: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, masquerading as apostles of Christ.
units.rightText: For such men are false apostles, deceitful workers, fashioning themselves into apostles of Christ.

units.leftText: And no wonder, for Satan himself masquerades as an angel of light.
units.rightText: And no marvel; for even Satan fashioneth himself into an angel of light.

units.leftText: It is not surprising, then, if his servants masquerade as servants of righteousness. Their end will correspond to their actions. Paul’s Suffering and Service (Colossians 1:24–29|COL 1:24-29*)
units.rightText: It is no great thing therefore if his ministers also fashion themselves as ministers of righteousness; whose end shall be according to their works.

units.leftText: I repeat: Let no one take me for a fool. But if you do, then receive me as a fool, so that I too may boast a little.
units.rightText: I say again, Let no man think me foolish; but if ye do, yet as foolish receive me, that I also may glory a little.

units.leftText: In this confident boasting of mine, I am not speaking as the Lord would, but as a fool.
units.rightText: That which I speak, I speak not after the Lord, but as in foolishness, in this confidence of glorying.

units.leftText: Since many are boasting according to the flesh, I too will boast.
units.rightText: Seeing that many glory after the flesh, I will glory also.

units.leftText: For you gladly put up with fools, since you are so wise.
units.rightText: For ye bear with the foolish gladly, being wise yourselves.

units.leftText: In fact, you even put up with anyone who enslaves you or exploits you or takes advantage of you or exalts himself or strikes you in the face.
units.rightText: For ye bear with a man, if he bringeth you into bondage, if he devoureth you, if he taketh you captive, if he exalteth himself, if he smiteth you on the face.

units.leftText: To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that!
units.rightText: I speak by way of disparagement, as though we had been weak. Yet whereinsoever any is bold (I speak in foolishness), I am bold also.

units.leftText: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they descendants of Abraham? So am I.
units.rightText: Are they Hebrews? so am I. Are they Israelites? so am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? so am I.

units.leftText: Are they servants of Christ? (I am speaking as if I were out of my mind.) I am so much more: in harder labor, in more imprisonments, in worse beatings, in frequent danger of death.
units.rightText: Are they ministers of Christ? (I speak as one beside himself) I more; in labors more abundantly, in prisons more abundantly, in stripes above measure, in deaths oft.

units.leftText: Five times I received from the Jews the forty lashes minus one.
units.rightText: Of the Jews five times received I forty stripes save one.

units.leftText: Three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I was shipwrecked. I spent a night and a day in the open sea.
units.rightText: Thrice was I beaten with rods, once was I stoned, thrice I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day have I been in the deep;

units.leftText: In my frequent journeys, I have been in danger from rivers and from bandits, in danger from my countrymen and from the Gentiles, in danger in the city and in the country, in danger on the sea and among false brothers,
units.rightText: in journeyings often, in perils of rivers, in perils of robbers, in perils from my countrymen, in perils from the Gentiles, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils in the sea, in perils among false brethren;

units.leftText: in labor and toil and often without sleep, in hunger and thirst and often without food, in cold and exposure.
units.rightText: in labor and travail, in watchings often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.

units.leftText: Apart from these external trials, I face daily the pressure of my concern for all the churches.
units.rightText: Besides those things that are without, there is that which presseth upon me daily, anxiety for all the churches.

units.leftText: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is led into sin, and I do not burn with grief?
units.rightText: Who is weak, and I am not weak? who is caused to stumble, and I burn not?

units.leftText: If I must boast, I will boast of the things that show my weakness.
units.rightText: If I must needs glory, I will glory of the things that concern my weakness.

units.leftText: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is forever worthy of praise, knows that I am not lying.
units.rightText: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, he who is blessed for evermore knoweth that I lie not.

units.leftText: In Damascus, the governor under King Aretas secured the city of the Damascenes in order to arrest me.
units.rightText: In Damascus the governor under Aretas the king guarded the city of the Damascenes in order to take me:

units.leftText: But I was lowered in a basket through a window in the wall and escaped his grasp.
units.rightText: and through a window was I let down in a basket by the wall, and escaped his hands.

units.leftText: I must go on boasting. Although there is nothing to gain, I will go on to visions and revelations from the Lord.
units.rightText: I must needs glory, though it is not expedient; but I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.

units.leftText: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago was caught up to the third heaven. Whether it was in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows.
units.rightText: I know a man in Christ, fourteen years ago (whether in the body, I know not; or whether out of the body, I know not; God knoweth), such a one caught up even to the third heaven.

units.leftText: And I know that this man— whether in the body or out of it I do not know, but God knows—
units.rightText: And I know such a man (whether in the body, or apart from the body, I know not; God knoweth),

units.leftText: was caught up to Paradise. The things he heard were inexpressible, things that man is not permitted to tell. Paul’s Thorn and God’s Grace
units.rightText: how that he was caught up into Paradise, and heard unspeakable words, which it is not lawful for a man to utter.

units.leftText: I will boast about such a man, but I will not boast about myself, except in my weaknesses.
units.rightText: On behalf of such a one will I glory: but on mine own behalf I will not glory, save in my weaknesses.

units.leftText: Even if I wanted to boast, I would not be a fool, because I would be speaking the truth. But I refrain, so no one will credit me with more than he sees in me or hears from me,
units.rightText: For if I should desire to glory, I shall not be foolish; for I shall speak the truth: but I forbear, lest any man should account of me above that which he seeth me to be, or heareth from me.

units.leftText: or because of these surpassingly great revelations.
units.rightText: And by reason of the exceeding greatness of the revelations, that I should not be exalted overmuch, there was given to me a thorn in the flesh, a messenger of Satan to buffet me, that I should not be exalted overmuch.

units.leftText: Three times I pleaded with the Lord to take it away from me.
units.rightText: Concerning this thing I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.

units.leftText: But He said to me, “My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is perfected in weakness.” Therefore I will boast all the more gladly in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest on me.
units.rightText: And he hath said unto me, My grace is sufficient for thee: for my power is made perfect in weakness. Most gladly therefore will I rather glory in my weaknesses, that the power of Christ may rest upon me.

units.leftText: That is why, for the sake of Christ, I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in hardships, in persecutions, in difficulties. For when I am weak, then I am strong. Paul’s Concern for the Corinthians
units.rightText: Wherefore I take pleasure in weaknesses, in injuries, in necessities, in persecutions, in distresses, for Christ’s sake: for when I am weak, then am I strong.

units.leftText: I have become a fool, but you drove me to it. In fact, you should have commended me, since I am in no way inferior to those “super-apostles,” even though I am nothing.
units.rightText: I am become foolish: ye compelled me; for I ought to have been commended of you: for in nothing was I behind the very chiefest apostles, though I am nothing.

units.leftText: The marks of a true apostle — signs, wonders, and miracles — were performed among you with great perseverance.
units.rightText: Truly the signs of an apostle were wrought among you in all patience, by signs and wonders and mighty works.

units.leftText: In what way were you inferior to the other churches, except that I was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
units.rightText: For what is there wherein ye were made inferior to the rest of the churches, except it be that I myself was not a burden to you? forgive me this wrong.

units.leftText: See, I am ready to come to you a third time, and I will not be a burden, because I am not seeking your possessions, but you. For children should not have to save up for their parents, but parents for their children.
units.rightText: Behold, this is the third time I am ready to come to you; and I will not be a burden to you: for I seek not yours, but you: for the children ought not to lay up for the parents, but the parents for the children.

units.leftText: And for the sake of your souls, I will most gladly spend my money and myself. If I love you more, will you love me less?
units.rightText: And I will most gladly spend and be spent for your souls. If I love you more abundantly, am I loved the less?

units.leftText: Be that as it may, I was not a burden to you; but crafty as I am, I caught you by trickery.
units.rightText: But be it so, I did not myself burden you; but, being crafty, I caught you with guile.

units.leftText: Did I exploit you by anyone I sent you?
units.rightText: Did I take advantage of you by any one of them whom I have sent unto you?

units.leftText: I urged Titus to visit you, and I sent our brother with him. Did Titus exploit you in any way? Did we not walk in the same Spirit and follow in the same footsteps?
units.rightText: I exhorted Titus, and I sent the brother with him. Did Titus take any advantage of you? walked we not in the same spirit? walked we not in the same steps?
leftNotes: 12:18 Literally Did we not walk in the same Spirit? Not in the same footsteps?

units.leftText: Have you been thinking all along that we were making a defense to you? We speak before God in Christ, and all of this, beloved, is to build you up.
units.rightText: Ye think all this time that we are excusing ourselves unto you. In the sight of God speak we in Christ. But all things, beloved, are for your edifying.

units.leftText: For I am afraid that when I come, I may not find you as I wish, and you may not find me as you wish. I fear that there may be quarreling, jealousy, rage, rivalry, slander, gossip, arrogance, and disorder.
units.rightText: For I fear, lest by any means, when I come, I should find you not such as I would, and should myself be found of you such as ye would not; lest by any means there should be strife, jealousy, wraths, factions, backbitings, whisperings, swellings, tumults;

units.leftText: I am afraid that when I come again, my God will humble me before you, and I will be grieved over many who have sinned earlier and have not repented of their acts of impurity, sexual immorality, and debauchery.
units.rightText: lest again when I come my God should humble me before you, and I should mourn for many of them that have sinned heretofore, and repented not of the uncleanness and fornication and lasciviousness which they committed.

units.leftText: This is the third time I am coming to you. “Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.”
units.rightText: This is the third time I am coming to you. At the mouth of two witnesses or three shall every word be established.

units.leftText: I already warned you the second time I was with you. So now in my absence I warn those who sinned earlier and everyone else: If I return, I will not spare anyone,
units.rightText: I have said beforehand, and I do say beforehand, as when I was present the second time, so now, being absent, to them that have sinned heretofore, and to all the rest, that, if I come again, I will not spare;

units.leftText: since you are demanding proof that Christ is speaking through me. He is not weak in dealing with you but is powerful among you.
units.rightText: seeing that ye seek a proof of Christ that speaketh in me; who to you-ward is not weak, but is powerful in you:

units.leftText: For He was indeed crucified in weakness, yet He lives by God’s power. For we are also weak in Him, yet by God’s power we will live with Him concerning you.
units.rightText: for he was crucified through weakness, yet he liveth through the power of God. For we also are weak in him, but we shall live with him through the power of God toward you.

units.leftText: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Do you not realize that Jesus Christ is in you — unless you fail the test?
units.rightText: Try your own selves, whether ye are in the faith; prove your own selves. Or know ye not as to your own selves, that Jesus Christ is in you? unless indeed ye be reprobate.

units.leftText: And I hope you will realize that we have not failed the test.
units.rightText: But I hope that ye shall know that we are not reprobate.

units.leftText: Now we pray to God that you will not do anything wrong — not that we will appear to have stood the test, but that you will do what is right, even if we appear to have failed.
units.rightText: Now we pray to God that ye do no evil; not that we may appear approved, but that ye may do that which is honorable, though we be as reprobate.

units.leftText: For we cannot do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
units.rightText: For we can do nothing against the truth, but for the truth.

units.leftText: In fact, we rejoice when we are weak but you are strong, and our prayer is for your perfection.
units.rightText: For we rejoice, when we are weak, and ye are strong: this we also pray for, even your perfecting.

units.leftText: This is why I write these things while absent, so that when I am present I will not need to be severe in my use of the authority that the Lord gave me for building you up, not for tearing you down. Benediction and Farewell
units.rightText: For this cause I write these things while absent, that I may not when present deal sharply, according to the authority which the Lord gave me for building up, and not for casting down.

units.leftText: Finally, brothers, rejoice! Aim for perfect harmony, encourage one another, be of one mind, live in peace. And the God of love and peace will be with you.
units.rightText: Finally, brethren, farewell. Be perfected; be comforted; be of the same mind; live in peace: and the God of love and peace shall be with you.

units.leftText: Greet one another with a holy kiss.
units.rightText: Salute one another with a holy kiss.

units.leftText: All the saints send you greetings.
units.rightText: All the saints salute you.

units.leftText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.
units.rightText: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit, be with you all.
leftNotes: 13:14 Texts vary in verse numbering for the last three verses of this chapter. BYZ ends with Amen.
